topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Single File' in the manual's group riding hand signals?
choice_a: Arm extended straight down, palm facing back
choice_b: Arm and index finger extended straight up
choice_c: Arm extended straight out, palm facing up, swinging upward
choice_d: Tapping the top of the helmet with an open palm
explanation: The manual's hand signal chart shows 'Single File' as the arm and index finger extended straight up.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: How does the 'Double File' hand signal differ from the 'Single File' signal?
choice_a: Double File and Single File use exactly the same gesture
choice_b: Double File is signaled entirely with the foot, not the hand
choice_c: Double File uses the arm with the index and middle finger extended straight up, rather than just the index finger
choice_d: Double File uses a closed fist held overhead
explanation: The manual distinguishes 'Double File' from 'Single File' by using the arm with the index and middle finger extended straight up, compared to just the index finger for single file.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Stop' in the manual's group riding signals?
choice_a: Arm extended straight up from the shoulder, palm forward
choice_b: Fist clenched with a short up-and-down motion
choice_d: Arm extended straight down, palm facing back
explanation: The manual shows the 'Stop' hand signal as the arm extended straight down, with the palm facing back.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Speed Up'?
choice_a: Arm extended straight out, palm facing up, swinging upward
choice_b: Arm extended straight out, palm facing down, swinging down to your side
choice_c: Open and close the hand with fingers and thumb extended
choice_d: Point with the left hand toward the hazard
explanation: The manual shows the 'Speed Up' signal as the arm extended straight out, palm facing up, swinging upward.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Slow Down'?
choice_a: Arm extended straight out, palm facing up, swinging upward
choice_b: Arm extended straight out, palm facing down, swinging down to your side
choice_c: Arm extended straight down with palm facing forward
choice_d: Tap on top of the helmet with an open palm
explanation: The manual shows the 'Slow Down' signal as the arm extended straight out, palm facing down, swung down to the side -- the mirror-image gesture of 'Speed Up.'
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Follow Me'?
choice_a: Arm extended upward 45 degrees, palm forward, pointing with the index finger, swinging in an arc from back to front
choice_b: Arm extended straight down, palm facing back
choice_c: Arm extended straight up from the shoulder, palm forward
choice_d: Forearm extended, fist clenched, with a short up-and-down motion
explanation: The manual shows the 'Follow Me' signal as the arm extended straight up from the shoulder, with the palm forward.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: How does the manual describe signaling a road hazard when it is on the right side of the lane?
choice_b: Tap the top of the helmet with an open palm
choice_c: Right-side hazards are not signaled at all
explanation: The manual's 'Hazard in Roadway' signal specifies that a hazard on the left is pointed to with the left hand, while a hazard on the right is pointed to with the right foot.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Highbeam'?
choice_a: Tap on top of the helmet with an open palm, palm down
choice_b: Open and close the hand with the fingers and thumb extended
choice_c: Point directly overhead with the index finger
explanation: The manual shows the 'Highbeam' signal as tapping on top of the helmet with an open palm facing down.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for a 'Refreshment Stop'?
choice_a: Forearm extended, fist clenched, with a short up-and-down motion
choice_c: Arm out to the side, pointing to the tank with a finger extended
choice_d: Open and close the hand with the fingers and thumb extended
explanation: The manual shows the 'Refreshment Stop' signal as fingers closed, thumb brought to the mouth -- distinct from the 'Comfort Stop' signal, which uses a clenched fist with an up-and-down motion.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Fuel', indicating a need to stop for gas?
choice_a: Fist clenched with a short up-and-down motion
choice_c: Arm out to the side, pointing to the tank with a finger extended
choice_d: Tap on top of the helmet with an open palm
explanation: The manual shows the 'Fuel' signal as the arm out to the side, pointing to the tank with a finger extended.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: What is the hand signal for 'Turn Signal On', used to alert a rider that their turn signal was left on?
choice_a: Point overhead with the index finger extended
choice_b: Tap the top of the helmet with an open palm
choice_c: Arm extended straight down, palm facing back
choice_d: Open and close the hand with fingers and thumb extended
explanation: The manual shows the 'Turn Signal On' signal as opening and closing the hand with the fingers and thumb extended.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.55, 'Hand Signals'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: In the Chassis ('C') section of the T-CLOCS pre-ride checklist, what should a rider check the steering-head bearings for?
choice_a: No detent or tight spots through the full range of travel, by raising the front wheel and checking for play by pulling and pushing the forks
choice_b: Only the color of the grease used on the bearings
choice_c: Steering-head bearings are not part of the T-CLOCS checklist
choice_d: Whether the bearings make noise while the engine idles
explanation: The T-CLOCS Chassis checklist instructs checking steering-head bearings for no detent or tight spots through full travel by raising the front wheel and checking for play by pulling and pushing the forks.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.56 (T-CLOCS Pre-Ride Inspection Checklist), 'C-Chassis'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: In the T-CLOCS checklist's Frame condition check, what should a rider look for at gussets and accessory mounts?
choice_a: Only whether the frame is a matching color to the rest of the motorcycle
choice_c: Frame condition is not part of the T-CLOCS checklist
choice_d: Only the presence of manufacturer decals
explanation: The T-CLOCS Chassis checklist instructs checking the frame's condition for cracks at gussets and accessory mounts, and watching for paint lifting as a sign of a developing crack.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.56 (T-CLOCS Pre-Ride Inspection Checklist), 'C-Chassis'

topic: Group Hand Signals and Pre-Ride Checklist
question: According to the T-CLOCS checklist, what should a rider check regarding the battery under the Lights (L) section?
choice_a: The battery only needs a visual check for its brand name
choice_b: Batteries are not addressed anywhere in the T-CLOCS checklist
choice_c: That the terminals are clean and tight, the electrolyte level is correct, and the battery is held down securely
choice_d: Only that the battery is fully charged, with no attention to terminals or mounting
explanation: The T-CLOCS Lights checklist instructs checking that battery terminals are clean and tight, the electrolyte level is correct, and the battery is held down securely.
source_note: MS Motorcycle Operator Manual (MSF 17th Ed.), p.56 (T-CLOCS Pre-Ride Inspection Checklist), 'L-Lights'
